NONE: › to become or make something become greater or more serious
（使）增強；（使）擴大；（使）加劇；（使）惡化

example: His financial problems escalated after he became unemployed.
他失業後，經濟問題更是雪上加霜。
The decision to escalate UN involvement has been made in the hopes of a swift end to the hostilities.
已決定加大聯合國介入的程度，以期盡快結束敵對。
The escalating rate of inflation will almost certainly bring escalating prices.
通貨膨脹率的不斷上升幾乎肯定會導致物價攀升。

NONE: B2 a set of stairs moved up or down by electric power on which people can stand and be taken from one level of a building to another, especially in shops, railway stations, and airports
自動手扶梯，電梯

example: I'll meet you by the up/down escalator on the second floor.
我會在三樓向上／下去的自動手扶梯旁跟你碰頭。

NONE: › a thin piece of meat without bones
薄肉片

example: veal/turkey escalopes
小牛／火雞肉片

NONE: › an act involving some danger, risk, or excitement, because it is different from usual or expected behaviour
冒險行爲；尋求刺激的行爲；惡作劇

example: Her latest escapade was to camp outside a department store on the night before the sale.
她最近的一個惡作劇是在一家百貨公司大減價的前一晚搭帳篷睡在店外。

I or T: B1 [ I or T ] to get free from something, or to avoid something
逃走，逃脫，逃離；逃避，避開

C or U: C1 [ C or U ] the act of successfully getting out of a place or a dangerous or bad situation

I: › [ I ] specialized computing to press the key on a computer keyboard that allows you to leave a particular screen and return to the previous one or to interrupt a process
退出，結束（電腦運行程式）

U: › [ U ] also escape key, written abbreviation Esc specialized the key on a computer keyboard that allows you to leave a particular screen and return to the previous one or to interrupt a process

C: › [ C ] a loss that happens by accident

S: B2 [ S ] something that helps you to forget about your usual life or problems
（對現實的）逃避，迴避；解脫之物：

example: Two prisoners have escaped.
兩個犯人逃走了。
A lion has escaped from its cage.
一頭獅子逃出了獸籠。
She was lucky to escape serious injury.
她真是萬幸，逃過一劫，沒有受重傷。
He narrowly (= only just) escaped a fine.
他差一點被罰款。
His name escapes me (= I have forgotten his name).
我記不起他的名字了。
Nothing important escapes her notice/attention.
任何重要的事情都不會逃過她的眼睛／注意。
Escape from this window and return to the main menu.
從這個視窗退出，返回主功能表。
He made his escape on the back of a motorcycle.
他騎上機車逃之夭夭。
an escape route
逃匿路線
They had a narrow escape (= only just avoided injury or death) when their car crashed.
撞車事故中，他們九死一生，逃過一劫。
an escape of radioactivity
放射線外泄
Romantic novels provide an escape from reality.
浪漫小說提供了一種逃避現實的方式。
Press Esc to return to the main menu.
按退出鍵返回主功能表。

NONE: › a person who entertains people by escaping from chains, boxes, etc.
表演脫逃的藝人，脫身術表演者
› the part of a submarine through which people can leave when it is underwater
（潛艇的）緊急出口
› a way of getting out of a difficult or unwanted situation
（擺脫困境等的）出路；（解決困難等的）辦法

example: The psychiatrist offered him an escape hatch from his feelings of guilt.
精神科醫師找到了辦法幫助他消除負罪感。

NONE: › See
escape noun(COMPUTER) ,
› having got free
逃脫了的；逃跑了的

example: an escaped prisoner
逃犯

NONE: › a person who has escaped from a place
逃離者；逃脫者

example: The escapees were recaptured after three days on the run.
這些人在脫逃三天後又重新被捕。

NONE: › a way of avoiding an unpleasant or boring life, especially by thinking, reading, etc. about more exciting but impossible activities
（尤指透過幻想、閱讀等達到的）逃避現實，解脫

example: These adventure movies are pure escapism.
這些冒險電影是純娛樂性的。
For many people going on holiday is a form of escapism.
對於很多人來說，度假是一種解脫方式。

NONE: › the activity of escaping from chains, boxes, etc. usually for entertainment
（通常作爲一種娛樂表演的）逃脫術，脫身術
› a steep slope or cliff, such as one that marks the edge of a range of hills
陡坡；懸崖；峭壁
› the part of theology (= the study of religion) that deals with death or the end of the world
終世論, 末世學
› to avoid something intentionally, or to give something up
迴避，避開；放棄

example: We won't have discussions with this group unless they eschew violence.
除非這個團體放棄使用暴力，否則我們不會與之舉行會談。

T: › to go with a person or vehicle, especially to make certain that he, she, or it leaves or arrives safely
（尤指爲了確保某人安全到達或離開某地）護衛，護送，押送
› to go with someone and show them a place
› formal to go to a social event with someone, especially a person of the opposite sex
陪伴（尤指異性）參加社交活動

C: › [ C ] a person who goes with another person as a partner to a social event
（通常指異性的）社交聚會陪伴者
› [ C ] someone who is paid to go out to social events with another person, and sometimes to have sex
受僱陪同某人外出社交的人（常指年輕女子）
› [ C ] a person or vehicle that goes somewhere with someone to protect or guard them
U: › [ U ] the state of having someone with you who gives you protection or guards you

example: Several little boats escorted the sailing ship into the harbour.
在數隻小船的護航下，帆船駛入海港。
Security guards escorted the intruders from the building.
保安把闖入者押送出了大樓。
The police escorted her to the airport, and made sure that she left the country.
警察將她押送到機場，確保其離境。
People on the tour will be escorted by an expert on archaeology.
遊客們將由一位考古學專家陪同前行。
Who will be escorting her to the ball?
誰將做她的舞伴呢？
"But I can't go to the dance without an escort," she protested.
「但是沒有舞伴我不能去參加舞會，」她抗議道。
He hired an escort to go to the dinner with him.
他僱了一位伴遊小姐陪他赴宴。
The members of the jury left the court with a police escort.
陪審團成員在警察的護送下離開了法庭。
The prisoners were transported under military escort.
這些犯人被軍人押送到流放地。

NONE: › a business that supplies people who work as escorts
伴遊公司
› an agreement between two people or organizations in which money or property is kept by a third person or organization until a particular condition is met
（在達成某種條件之前將錢款或財産交由第三方保管的）有待完成條件的合約（或契據）

example: The money was placed in escrow.
履行協定期間，這筆錢暂由第三方保管。

NONE: › the standard unit of money used in Portugal before the introduction of the euro, and in Cape Verde
（葡萄牙在使用歐元前的標準貨幣單位；佛得角標準貨幣單位）埃斯固多
